topic: Joint evaluation and selective prediction for temporally evolving multi-source generation: evidence completeness for compound and partially supported claims, longitudinal omission of superseded or due work-item state, and online calibration under non-stationary streams

open_gaps.description: No admitted study validates one end-to-end evaluation scheme that jointly measures claim correctness, evidence attribution correctness, citation or evidence completeness, temporal or current-state correctness, omission, calibrated uncertainty, and abstention while preserving separate denominators for those dimensions. The corpus validates individual components and smaller combinations.
open_gaps.suggested_search_query: "joint evaluation framework" factuality attribution completeness temporal correctness omission calibration abstention "free-form generation" multi-source
open_gaps.resolution_notes: Still open after rounds 1-4. Papers 2405.00982, 2509.26184, 2510.07238, 2606.29054, and 2607.19322 add component-level or partial combinations, but none validates the full joint evaluation scheme with separate denominators for all named dimensions.

open_gaps.description: The corpus contains no direct evaluation on private workplace email or Teams-style communication with realistic revisions, quoted history, conflicting updates, delayed or out-of-order arrival, versioned attachments, and permission-constrained evidence. Target-domain fixtures and gold data remain an engineering validation gap.
open_gaps.resolution_notes: Resolve by constructing a permission-safe target-domain benchmark or synthetic/replayed fixture suite covering email and Teams-style threads, quoted history, revision chains, contradictory updates, delayed and out-of-order arrival, attachment versions, and access-control boundaries. Define gold current-state records and evidence provenance, then benchmark the system against these fixtures with reproducible scripts and versioned datasets.

open_gaps.description: The corpus does not establish a general evidence-completeness method that jointly handles compound claims, partially supportive evidence, multiple complementary sources, and temporally versioned evidence. Separate studies cover subsets of these conditions.
open_gaps.suggested_search_query: "evidence completeness" compound claims partial support complementary evidence multi-source temporal versioning provenance evaluation
open_gaps.resolution_notes: Still open after rounds 1-4. Papers 2305.11859, 2404.15588, 2508.20867, doi-10-18653-v1-2025-acl-long-837, and doi-10-1109-access-2026-3679691 cover constituent problems such as decomposition, partial support, sufficient evidence, multi-source retrieval, or temporal validity, but no admitted method jointly addresses all conditions.

open_gaps.description: Report-level omission has substantial benchmark coverage, but the corpus still does not establish omission detection for evolving workplace work items, due information, superseded facts, or decision-relevant state across time.
open_gaps.suggested_search_query: "omission detection" longitudinal summarization work-item state superseded facts due dates temporal updates decision-relevant information
open_gaps.resolution_notes: Still open after rounds 1-4. Papers and resources 2405.00982, 2607.19322, doi-10-1155-2016-1340973, doi-10-6028-nist-sp-500-321-realtime-overview, and manual-39435af3dd address update summarization, novelty, redundancy, temporal update coverage, or factual completeness, but do not directly evaluate omission of evolving work-item obligations, due state, and supersession chains.

open_gaps.description: A target-domain human-review protocol remains an engineering gap: representative or risk-stratified sampling, minimum human-review volume, multi-rater adjudication, confusion matrices, abstention treatment, coverage reporting, and validation of any LLM-assisted judge against independent human judgments remain project-specific choices.
open_gaps.resolution_notes: Resolve by defining a documented validation protocol for the target system: establish representative and risk-stratified sampling frames; predefine sample-size or stopping criteria; use blinded independent raters with adjudication; report inter-rater agreement, confusion matrices, abstention and coverage separately; and validate any LLM-assisted judge against an independently labeled human holdout. Existing evidence including 2406.07967, 2605.16354, 2606.00093, manual-32d5793dca, and manual-f5ce52cae2 can inform the protocol but cannot determine project-specific thresholds.

open_gaps.description: The corpus demonstrates evaluator-optimization effects, rating indeterminacy, abstention sensitivity, and directional judge bias but does not provide a project-specific procedure for preventing acceptance criteria from being overfit to the same automatic evaluator used during development. Independent holdouts, evaluator separation, and regression checks remain an engineering validation problem.
open_gaps.resolution_notes: Resolve by separating development and acceptance evaluators, freezing an independent holdout set and scoring protocol, preventing development-time access to acceptance labels, periodically cross-checking automatic judges against blinded human judgments, maintaining evaluator-versioned regression suites, and requiring acceptance decisions to pass both fixed holdout and independent-human checks. Evidence including 2212.08037, 2606.00093, 2607.08700, and manual-32d5793dca motivates these controls but does not prescribe the project-specific procedure.

open_gaps.description: Calibration under continuing temporal or distributional change remains open for non-stationary free-form communication streams. The corpus supplies adaptive coverage results, cross-domain calibration studies, benchmark-aging evidence, and structured-generation risk-control results, but not one validated selective-prediction method for continuously changing workplace communication.
open_gaps.suggested_search_query: "selective prediction" "non-stationary" free-form generation online calibration concept drift abstention adaptive conformal temporal stream
open_gaps.resolution_notes: Still open after rounds 1-4. Papers 2106.00170, 2208.08401, 2302.07869, 2602.16537, and 2606.29054 provide evidence on adaptive or strongly adaptive conformal prediction, distribution shift, and structured-generation risk control, but none validates a selective-prediction method on continuously changing free-form workplace communication.
